## Supported host and working directory
Only DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 is supported. `spawn`, `stat`, and `list_dir` require the host working-directory
service, including directory changes and missing-directory recovery. Relative `cwd` overrides resol
ve against that current directory. The sandbox workspace root does not change. There is no older-hos
t service probe or workspace/header cwd fallback.
## Output encoding
`spawn` automatically decodes stdout and stderr independently on every OS. It captures raw pipes, re
cognizes UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32 BOMs, prefers strictly valid UTF-8, and otherwise detects a supported l
egacy encoding. High-confidence detection takes precedence over platform hints; ambiguous samples us
e Windows ACP/console/OEM code pages or the effective POSIX locale (`LC_ALL`, then `LC_CTYPE`, then
`LANG`). Locale hints reflect explicit child `env` overrides. No encoding environment variables, sys
tem code pages, target application settings, or tool-call encoding parameters are changed or added.
ASCII output is delivered immediately without locking a later non-ASCII line to UTF-8. Legacy detect
ion buffers at most 8 KiB and selects an encoding on a newline, the sample limit, or EOF, without a
timer; incomplete characters are carried across chunks. Short legacy output without a newline remain
s buffered until more bytes arrive or the stream ends. Foreground results and background readers sha
re the same decoding path. The output budget, reader byte offsets, and complete spill files use **no
rmalized UTF-8**, so spills can be read by ordinary UTF-8 file tools. Truncated tails drop an incomp
lete leading character rather than displaying a replacement caused by truncation.
Detection is heuristic: very short ambiguous text or multiple encodings mixed in one stream cannot a
lways be identified. Programs producing binary output should write it to a file rather than relying
on this text tool. Windows native code-page lookup is optional metadata; decoding still works if it
ol. Windows native code-page lookup is optional metadata; decoding still works if it is unavailable.

`list_dir` uses ripgrep-style **project-level** filters by default. `ignore` and `hidden` are indepe

- `ignore` defaults to `true`: apply project ignore-file rules. Setting it to `false` does not enabl

e hidden entries and does not read ignore files.
- `hidden` defaults to `false`: skip dotfiles and d
ot-directories, including `.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.env` and `.cache`. Setting it to `true` does not
bypass ignore-file rules. When ignore rules are enabled, an explicit whitelist can still include a h
idden entry even with `hidden: false`.

behavior is unchanged in this patch: entries are skipped while `ignore` is true; with `ignore: fals
e`, the underlying host listing/traversal behavior is preserved. No separate link-following option i

Glob parsing reuses the npm `ignore` package. Conflicting rules use `.rgignore` > `.ignore` > `.giti
gnore` > `.git/info/exclude` precedence, regardless of directory depth; within one source type, deep
er rules win. Git rules require a repository (`.git` or `.jj`), and stop at nested repository bounda
ries. Parent `.ignore` and `.rgignore` files continue across repository boundaries. Worktree/submodu
le Git metadata and shared `commondir` exclude files are supported. Ignored directories are pruned b
efore recursion and do not consume the 2000-entry limit. Rules inside pruned directories cannot reop
en them. As with rg, explicitly requested starting directories are traversed even if hidden or ignor
them. As with rg, explicitly requested starting directories are traversed even if hidden or ignored.
All filesystem access uses the host `ctx.fs` service; symlinked rule files are not followed. This is
not full ripgrep compatibility: rules are case-sensitive, hidden means dot-prefixed (Windows hidden
attributes are unavailable), global Git configuration/excludes and per-user ripgrep configuration a
re not loaded, and the tracked-file index is not consulted. This directory-listing tool does not ins
pect file contents or filter binary files. Tests compare supported project filtering against a real
`rg --files` binary when available.

## Tools and preset
`spawn` requires the `jobs`, `sandbox`, `sandboxPolicy`, and `workingDirectory` services. Every invo
cation starts a job; foreground calls wait for completion and move the job to the background on time
out. Infrastructure failures throw in foreground calls and settle background jobs as `failed`; nonze
ro command exits remain ordinary results.
The `@snylonue/dsh-spawn` entry registers only `spawn`. Load `@snylonue/dsh-spawn/stat` and `@snylon
ue/dsh-spawn/list-dir` separately for filesystem queries. The `PTC-spawn` preset enables all three b
y default. To disable either query tool in that preset, set `disabled: true` on its entry under `pre
set-ptc-spawn.config.plugins`:
